subject: Production: p99 latency spike + token/sec drop (QuickCommerce)
messages:
From: Sam Reynolds <sam@quickcommerce.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Production: p99 latency spike + token/sec drop (QuickCommerce)

Ava / Rishi,

We're seeing a sharp regression in p95/p99 latency and a drop in tokens/sec on the Hosted API that started ~04:15 UTC this morning. Affected routes: /v1/generate (model: rwd-open-65b).

Symptoms: 
- p95 went from ~220ms -> 1.4s, p99 ~2.8s.
- Our downstream TPS (tokens/sec) collapsed by ~45% at the same time.
- Error rate for 5xx increased from 0.2% -> 1.6% (spiky).

This correlates with the deploy note we got at 04:00 UTC about a quant/profile update — not sure if that's causal. We've captured a short dashboard screenshot and a few request ids: req_8a7f, req_8a93, req_8b10.

We need an urgent triage call and either a rollback or immediate mitigation. This is impacting checkout flows for some customers. Please advise ETA.

Attached: quickcommerce-p99-screenshot.png

--
Sam Reynolds
Head of Platform Reliability
QuickCommerce

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: p99 latency spike + token/sec drop (QuickCommerce)

Sam — thanks for the callout and the request ids. We're treating this as P1.

Immediate steps we've kicked off: 
- Triage checklist started and oncall is running targeted logs for the given request ids.
- Preparing an emergency policy to route QuickCommerce traffic to a pre-quantized fp16 variant to test whether quant rollout is the culprit.
- Asking infra to confirm whether kernel-selector changes landed in the host pool that serves rwd-open-65b around 03:50–04:10 UTC.

Can you send any additional sample input payloads (if available) and confirm whether the spike coincided with a high burst of bot traffic? We'll propose a short mitigation (fallback to fp16 variant + temporarily widen autoscale).

I'll follow up within 45 minutes with next steps and an invite for a short triage session.

Attached: initial-triage-checklist.txt

—Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: infra-oncall@redwood.com, runtime-team@redwood.com
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: p99 latency spike + token/sec drop (QuickCommerce)

Team — assigning a focused investigation. Notes from initial read: 
- Timeline: our deploy/rollout logs show a scheduled quant/profile change pushed at 03:49:12 UTC (job quant-rollout-20270504).
- Kernel-selector binary (qselect v2.1.7) also had a light rollout yesterday; need to check backcompat with rwd-open-65b in q4 quant mode.

Hypothesis A (high probability): a quant profile change triggered a different kernel path that increases per-token latency for long-sequence requests, and this cascaded into lower tokens/sec (because latency per token increased).
Hypothesis B: unrelated infra contention causing intermittent 5xx and autoscaler thrash.

Immediate asks for runtime/infra: 
1) Retrieve kernel selection logs for the pool serving QC traffic between 03:30–05:00 UTC. Look for kernel id mapping changes and any Fallback->SlowKernel events.
2) Compare perf for the same model on q8 vs q4 quant profiles for a 1024-token seq. Run reproducer job on a replica.
3) If reproducer shows the same throughput drop, prepare a quick rollback plan for the quant profile and a kernel-selector pin to the previous binary.

I've attached a short diff of the config we pushed this morning (kernel-config-diff.patch) — the change is small but likely influential (kernel preference list reorder). Please update this thread with artifacts and perf numbers.

-Rishi
VP, Serving Runtime
From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@quickcommerce.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: p99 latency spike + token/sec drop (QuickCommerce)

Sam — quick update from the triage call (summary and short mitigation applied):

What we found (quick): 
- Kernel selector logs show a preference reorder that caused a subset of inference workers to pick an experimental kernel path for q4 quant profiles at 03:50 UTC.
- Reproducer runs mirrored the customer symptom: q4 + experimental kernel -> ~40–55% TPS reduction for 1024-token loads. q8 and the previous kernel are within expected baselines.

Mitigation applied (11:00 UTC): 
- Enabled automatic fallback for QuickCommerce to the pinned kernel path (previous default) and temporarily switched their traffic to the fp16 model variant while we confirm stability for q4.
- Autoscale policy widened to add headroom for the next 30 minutes.

Result so far: p95/p99 recovering on our side; quick internal numbers show tokens/sec for sampled requests improved from 55 TPS -> ~95 TPS for the same batch. We'll monitor for 2 hours and then discuss a permanent fix.

Can you confirm whether you see improvement on your dashboard? If so, we will schedule a post-mortem to produce an RCA and discuss credits.
